name: Spoons
description: Spoons (also known as Tongue or Pig) is a fast-paced shedding and elimination game played with a standard card deck and a set of spoons (one less than the number of players). The objective is to collect four of a kind (e.g., four 6s) and then grab a spoon. As soon as one spoon is taken, everyone else must grab a spoon. The person left without a spoon is eliminated or receives a letter (S-P-O-O-N).

overview.description: Spoons (also known as Tongue or Pig) is a fast-paced shedding and elimination game played with a standard card deck and a set of spoons (one less than the number of players). The objective is to collect four of a kind (e.g., four 6s) and then grab a spoon. As soon as one spoon is taken, everyone else must grab a spoon. The person left without a spoon is eliminated or receives a letter (S-P-O-O-N).

history.origins: A family of simple card-passing games played in a circle; players pass one card left and try to collect four of a kind. The group has no single documented inventor. Pig uses a nose-touch signal; Spoons uses one fewer spoon than players in the center. Regional variants include Bouchon (France, with corks), Donkey (Australia, sometimes called Hog), Vatra and Magarac (Bosnia and Herzegovina), and Popa Prostul (Romania). More dangerous variants use forks or knives instead of spoons. Widely played as a parlor and children's game, with many contributors to the documented rules.
timeline: 1950s: Becomes a staple at summer camps.
1990s: Played as a drinking game in colleges.
history.cultural: Known for chaotic scrambles and bruised knuckles.
history.evolution: The use of 'Spoons' is arbitrary; it could be pens, coins, or anything grab-able.

setup.players: 2 to 13 (up to 13 with one 52-card pack; more with multiple packs).
setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack, or multiple packs for more than 12 players.
setup.dealing: Four cards dealt to each player clockwise. Remainder forms the stock to dealer's right (stock version), or use four cards of one rank per player with no stock.
setup.equipment: One spoon fewer than the number of players, placed in the center where any player can reach.

rules.objective: Collect four cards of the same rank, then take a spoon. Do not be the last player without a spoon.
rules.gameplay: Players pass one card face down to their left-hand neighbour at a time (and in the stock version the dealer draws from the stock while the player to dealer's right discards to a pile). Passing continues until someone collects four of a kind. That player takes a spoon from the center; as soon as one spoon is taken, all other players may grab a spoon. One fewer spoon than players, so one player loses the deal. Loser gets a letter (e.g. S-P-O-O-N) or is eliminated; remove one spoon per eliminated player.
keyRules: Pass exactly one card at a time to the left; never hold more than four cards.
First to collect four of a kind takes a spoon; then everyone may grab a spoon.
Last player without a spoon loses the deal.
When stock is exhausted, shuffle the discard pile to form a new stock.

strategy.basic: Keep your eyes on the spoons, not just your cards. If you see movement in the center, grab first, ask questions later. Don't hold disparate cards; focus on one rank early (e.g., if you have two 5s, discard everything else to find the other two 5s).
strategy.intermediate: The 'Sneaky' Grab: If you get 4 of a kind, quietly take a spoon without anyone noticing. Continue playing/passing cards with one hand while holding the spoon. Watch the chaos unfold as others realize slowly.
strategy.advanced: The 'Fake' Reach: Reach towards the spoons to make everyone panic-grab. Rules often penalize this (e.g., you lose a life if you touch a spoon without 4 of a kind). Use with caution.

variations.name: With stock pile
variations.description: Full 52-card deck; four cards each, remainder forms stock to dealer's right. Dealer draws from stock; player to dealer's right discards to a discard pile. When stock is exhausted, shuffle discard to form new stock.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes stock vs no-stock; engine phases and actions apply to both.

variations.name: Without stock pile
variations.description: Use four cards of one rank per player (e.g. 16 cards for 4 players: aces, kings, queens, jacks). No stock; all players pass one card left simultaneously. First to collect four of a kind takes a spoon.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes stock vs no-stock; engine phases and actions apply to both.

scoring.description: Collect 4 of a kind. Don't be the last to grab a spoon.
scoring.winCondition: Collect 4 of a kind. Don't be the last to grab a spoon.
